incident: FIN13 (Elephant Beetle) intrusion against a bank in Peru - Case 2

sources.title: Mandiant - FIN13 blog
sources.what_it_gave: Log4j DMZ breach, SharePoint pivot, LSASS dumps, domain-admin creds, DC + SecurID

sources.title: Sygnia - Elephant Beetle
sources.what_it_gave: AKATWEB webshell, SharePoint RCE, PsExec RDP enablement, SecurID VM cloning, fraud

sources.title: FIN13 Case 2 Attack Flow (CTID corpus)
sources.what_it_gave: Log4j -> AKATWEB -> SharePoint -> DC -> INTSRV/V-Center -> SecurID clone

narrative_before: FIN13 breached a bank in Peru (reported January 2022) by exploiting the Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) on an internet-facing proxy web server (AKATWEB) in the DMZ and implanting a JSP webshell (Mandiant, Sygnia). They moved laterally to a DMZ SharePoint server, likely via the SharePoint RCE CVE-2019-0604, and dumped cached SharePoint credentials from LSASS to crack offline, obtaining domain-admin credentials for SQL servers. Using valid accounts they logged into databases, identified a domain controller, and used PsExec (with a batch script, CCfix.bat, enabling RDP on four hosts) to reach it. They then moved to the INTSRV area hosting SecurID servers and a VMware vCenter, cloned a SecurID server VM, exported its image over the webshell, and used the SecurID clone with stolen accounts to commit fraud against mobile-banking users.

detection_moments.description: Initial access: Log4j (CVE-2021-44228) exploited on the AKATWEB proxy server, JSP webshell implanted.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Exploited the Log4j vulnerability to open a breach head on the DMZ ... Implanted a JSP webshell' - CTID flow / Mandiant

detection_moments.description: Lateral movement to the SharePoint server (RCE), LSASS dump yielding domain-admin creds, then PsExec to the domain controller.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Moved laterally to a DMZ segment hosting a SharePoint server ... dumped the SharePoint cached credentials ... Multiple instances of PsExec ... on the targeted DC' - CTID flow / Sygnia

detection_moments.description: Movement into the INTSRV area, access to vCenter with stolen accounts, and cloning/export of a SecurID server VM before fraud.
detection_moments.evidence: 'accessed the V-Center server using previously stolen valid accounts ... cloned one of the SecurID servers ... exported the SecurID server image over the webshell' - CTID flow / Sygnia

attack_path: RCE (likely CVE-2019-0604) to DMZ SharePoint server - T1203
PsExec with cracked domain-admin credentials to the domain controller - T1569.002 / T1078
valid accounts used to reach INTSRV VMware vCenter - T1078
SecurID server VM cloned and image exported over webshell - T1111 / T1041
ambiguities: Entry (Log4j) dates to late 2021; the report was published January 2022 - year set to 2021 (intrusion year).
equipos.txt lists four RDP-enabled hosts (QTCBDC02, QTVCTR01, QTBKSR02, QTJPGPA1); modelled by role (dc, vcenter) rather than all four to respect 'do not invent' and the role mapping.
